hook_text: A snake has no legs, a fish has no ears you can see, and a bat hears in the dark. So what do all animals share?
clip_script: Zoo day in Johannesburg! Every animal has a plan: head, body, tail, limbs. The lion swishes its tail at flies. The ostrich runs on two legs but cannot fly. The snake? No limbs at all. Now senses: the zebra's eyes are on the sides, so it can see the lion sneaking up. The elephant smells with its trunk. The beetle feels with its antennae. And coverings: fur, feathers, scales, shells, wet skin. Same plan, wildly different animals.
visual_style: Whiteboard outline of a dog labelled head, body, tail and limbs, then a row of animals with fur, feathers, scales and shells.
mood: Lively and amazed, like a walk through the zoo.
pacing: Label one animal fast, then a parade of animals showing how the same parts look different.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and label the head, body, tail and limbs of a pet or a bird near you.
